articleOfWeek.title: Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
articleOfWeek.abstract: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA. A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: Background High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. Purpose We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). Methods We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. Results We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99 th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Conclusion Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.

articles.title: Heat Stroke Cooling Devices for Prehospital Use: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Heat stroke and heat exhaustion (HS/HE) are life-threatening conditions requiring immediate intervention. Cooling devices play a critical role in emergency and prehospital care, yet their effectiveness and field readiness are inconsistently reported. This systematic review evaluates commercially available cooling devices for the treatment of HS/HE with an emphasis on device feasibility, performance, and suitability for prehospital and remote deployment. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in August/October 2025 across academic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Compendex, Engineering Village, and IEEE Xplore) and gray literature via Google Advanced Search. Academic records were screened using Rayyan, while gray literature was organized in Excel with the aid of a custom HTML scraper. Devices were included if they met the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) definition of a medical device, were designed for adult human use, and specifically addressed HS/HE. Parameters extracted included working principle, cooling rate, weight, dimensions, volume, power requirements, external resource demands, and reusability. Cooling performance was benchmarked using thresholds reported by McDermott, et al, and portability was assessed using the MIL-STD-1472H single-person carriage limit of ≤16kg. A total of 18 devices were identified and evaluated. Only three met the ideal cooling rate threshold (≥0.155°C/minute), and two others achieved acceptable performance (0.078-0.154°C/minute). Approximately 61% of devices did not report cooling rate data. Five devices met field portability criteria (≤16kg), though most were limited by reliance on water, power, or disposable components. Only one device demonstrated feasibility for remote use; this device, however, lacked full reusability. No device meets the combined criteria of effectiveness, portability, field readiness, and reusability for HS/HE treatment. Current FDA pathways do not require reporting of key performance metrics, highlighting a regulatory gap. There is a need for development of field-appropriate solutions and revised evaluation standards that prioritize cooling performance, resource independence, and usability in austere environments.

articles.title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia after traumatic brain injury: a timing-sensitive ecological framework of neuroimmune-pulmonary vulnerability.
articles.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is frequent after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its biological meaning and outcome impact remain incompletely defined. Traditional models emphasise mechanical ventilation, aspiration, colonisation, endotracheal tube biofilm, and hospital pathogens. These mechanisms remain essential, but they do not fully explain the early clustering, heterogeneous susceptibility, changing bacteriology, and variable mortality effect observed after TBI. Severe brain injury creates an early vulnerable host state through impaired consciousness and airway protection, neuroimmune dysregulation, autonomic and endocrine activation, altered pulmonary immune surveillance, and, in many patients, extracranial trauma, shock, transfusion, or thoracic injury. These processes interact with ventilation, antibiotic pressure, and rapid respiratory microbiome disruption. Early VAP may reflect abrupt loss of control after injury and intubation, whereas late VAP may reflect persistent or secondary failure driven by biofilm maturation, antibiotic selection, multidrug-resistant pathogens, and intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired immune dysfunction. Clinically, VAP consistently prolongs ventilation, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and resource use, while its independent effect on mortality is phenotype- and context-dependent. This model proposes a timing-sensitive ecological framework in which established mechanisms may converge early and with particular clinical intensity after severe TBI, creating a vulnerable host-microbe state that may lower the threshold for clinically apparent infection. Future studies should distinguish isolated TBI from polytrauma, compare TBI with other acute brain injuries and non-neurological ventilated populations, and incorporate dynamic immune, microbial, and trajectory-based outcomes. VAP after TBI should be viewed as a timing-sensitive interaction between ventilator exposure and early host vulnerability, not as a distinct disease entity or as a pneumonia pathway unique to traumatic brain injury. The TBI-focused contribution lies in the early convergence of otherwise non-unique mechanisms: impaired airway control, aspiration risk, neuroimmune-endocrine activation, treatment exposure, dysbiosis, and extracranial injury burden, rather than in any single TBI-specific mechanism. Isolated TBI and TBI with polytrauma are biologically different phenotypes and should be separated in future studies. Early and late VAP may represent different phases of loss of pulmonary host-microbe containment; this distinction is probabilistic rather than TBI-specific in itself and requires validation in TBI-stratified cohorts. Mortality remains clinically relevant but context-dependent; VAP more consistently modifies recovery trajectory, ventilator dependence, ICU stay, antibiotic exposure, and possibly neurological recovery.

articles.title: Preserved anabolic skeletal muscle capacity in response to exercise and protein intake after critical illness.
articles.abstract: Low muscle mass and persistent weakness are common after critical illness, but the mechanisms behind impaired recovery are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. We hypothesised that residual anabolic resistance limits muscle regeneration after ICU stay. Former patients were enrolled within 3 to 6 months of intensive care unit discharge. Muscle biopsies were obtained before and after resistance exercise using a flywheel leg extension ergometer, combined with ingestion of 24 g hydrolysed protein. Muscle protein fractional synthetic rate was determined from the incorporation of [ring-²H₅]phenylalanine into mixed-muscle protein during a primed continuous intravenous infusion. Anabolic and proteolytic pathways were measured using standard assays. Group-by-time differences were analysed using linear mixed models. The primary comparison was the between-group difference in pre-to-post change in muscle protein synthesis. Twenty ICU survivors (60 ± 12 years, 30% female, BMI 26.9 (IQR 22.9-28.7), SAPS 3 62.3 ± 15.8) and 20 age- and sex-matched controls were included. ICU survivors had significantly lower quadriceps muscle thickness (p = 0.02) and handgrip strength (p = 0.04) than controls. In ICU survivors, muscle protein synthesis from plasma precursor amino acids was higher at baseline than in controls (0.041%/hour vs. 0.030%/hour, p = 0.009), but increased less (Δ 0.031 vs. Δ 0.040%/hour, p = 0.04). Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis was similar between groups (0.071%/hour vs. 0.070%/hour, p = 0.70). At baseline, ICU survivors showed lower activation of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In both groups, the intervention increased anabolic signalling, decreased initiation of autophagy and increased parts of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. In ICU survivors with persistent muscle loss and weakness, the increase in muscle protein synthesis after combined resistance exercise and protein intake was smaller than in controls, in the context of a higher baseline fractional synthetic rate. Post-intervention muscle protein synthesis rates were similar between groups. These findings provide the first mechanistic support for structured exercise-nutrition rehabilitation to promote muscle recovery after critical illness. This study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05261984), 2022-02-20.

Artificial Intelligence-Assisted, Electrocardiogram-Derived, Sequential Rule-Based Decision Tree for Exclusion of Acute Coronary Syndrome as the Etiology of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: After out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), deciding which patients without ST-segment elevation warrant emergency coronary angiography is difficult, as standard electrocardiogram (ECG), troponin, and echocardiography are limited in the early post-arrest window. We aimed to develop a sequential rule-based decision tree to identify post-ROSC patients in whom acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is unlikely to be the arrest etiology. In this single-center retrospective study, adult patients with OHCA were divided into development (2020-2024; n=329) and temporal validation (2025; n=71) cohorts. Post-ROSC 12-lead ECGs were analyzed by a deep-learning platform generating ten digital biomarkers. Five candidate biomarkers were combined into a rhythm-stratified sequential decision tree under a zero false-negative constraint; its performance was compared with that of individual biomarkers and validated in the temporal cohort. The tree classified 171/329 (52.0%) and 32/71 (45.1%) patients in the development and validation cohorts, respectively, as "ACS not likely," with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified at any node. Yield concentrated in the non-shockable subgroup, in which the model excluded 169/261 (64.8%) non-ACS cases (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC], 0.824), outperforming each individual biomarker. In the shockable subgroup, which carries a high pretest probability of ACS, 38/40 patients (95.0%) were retained as "ACS not excluded." A rhythm-stratified, rule-based decision tree combining AI-assisted ECG-derived biomarkers classified approximately half of post-OHCA patients as "ACS not likely" with no adjudicated ACS case misclassified, principally in the non-shockable subgroup. This transparent, bedside-deployable framework warrants prospective multicenter evaluation.

articles.title: Ventilation Monitoring in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Care.
articles.abstract: Adherence to American Heart Association (AHA) ventilation guidelines during cardiac arrest is challenging. Prospective, Before/After quality assurance study determining adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by Milwaukee County Emergency Medical Services and Kenosha Fire in Wisconsin using (Before) end tidal carbon dioxide [ETCO2] to monitor ventilations - Real BVM Help® applied but blinded versus (After) Real BVM Help®. mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in-target for rate, tidal volume, and both rate and tidal volume. AHA 2020 guidelines were followed. From 9/29/22-12/22/23, 278 patients were entered (148 Before/130 After). Average age: 62.3±16.7 years; 185 (67%) male. Mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in Before/After Groups in-target for rate (47.7±25.1% vs 74.4±24.1% respectively, p<0.0001), tidal volume (15.3±15.4% vs 45.4±23.8% respectively, p<0.0001), and rate and tidal volume (7.5±9.6% vs 39.0±23.3% respectively, p<0.0001) were significantly higher in the After Group. In the Before Group, using ETCO2 to monitor all ventilations (N=22,037 ventilations), only 43.8% were in-target for rate, 13.5% in-target for tidal volume, and 6.8% in-target for rate and tidal volume with a lower-than-target tidal volume delivered in 58.2% of all ventilations. Real BVM Help® was associated with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines. ETCO2 monitoring failed to approach both rate and tidal volume guideline adherence with a lower-than-target tidal volume being the most common parameter delivered out-of-target (58.2%). Ventilation rate and tidal volume monitoring with real-time feedback should be considered during treatment of cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Early Identification of Recurrent Out-of-hospital Cardiac Arrest Using Clinical ECG Features.
articles.abstract: Recurrent cardiac arrest (rearrest) after initial return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is associated with relatively poor outcomes. Early identification of rearrest might allow for intervention to prevent rearrest. In this study, we sought to determine whether clinical ECG features can predict rearrest. We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients who achieved ROSC between 2018-2024. We evaluated the association of ECG features (QRS width, standard deviation of NN intervals, root mean square of successive NN interval differences, and percentage of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 milliseconds) within individual 15-second segments throughout a 5-minute window prior to rearrest as well as their temporal trends over the 5-minute analytic window. Of the 1,489 OHCA patients achieving ROSC, 1,298 were analyzed; 528 (40.7%) experienced rearrest. Rearrest patients were older, less likely to receive bystander CPR (48.7% vs. 61.9%), and had lower survival (20.4% vs. 43.1%) and favorable neurologic outcomes (7.8% vs. 21.2%; all p<0.001). We found lower heart rate, wider QRS, and higher HR variability in those with rearrest. Identification was highest 1 minute prior to rearrest (AUROC 0.74), declining beyond 3 minutes. Models using temporal trends achieved AUROC 0.67; strongest predictors were heart rate variability measures and QRS width. Established ECG features achieved good prediction for rearrest with identification improving closer to time of rearrest. Future work leveraging novel features or more advanced artificial intelligence models may further improve prediction.

articles.title: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID). SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles. In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

articles.title: Epidemiological Study on Tranexamic Acid Use in Pediatric Blunt Liver and Spleen Injuries in Japan: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Blunt abdominal trauma is a leading cause of pediatric morbidity, yet tranexamic acid (TXA) use remains scarce compared to adult care. This study assessed TXA's efficacy in pediatric patients with blunt hepatic and splenic injuries. This retrospective multicenter study in Japan (2008-2019) evaluated patients aged ≤16 years admitted for blunt hepatic or splenic injuries of grade 1 or higher, according to the American Association for the Surgery of Trauma Organ Injury Scale. We investigated clinical outcomes associated with TXA administration. Among 1,406 eligible patients, 282 (20.1%) received TXA, primarily those with severe injuries. Administration occurred within 1 h of injury in 32.3%, 1-3 h in 31.2%, and after 3 h in 35.1%. No side effects were reported. However, TXA was not significantly associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.67, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.16-2.79, p=0.58), red blood cell transfusion volume (coefficient -6.76, 95% CI -18.6 to 5.11, p=0.26), total transfusion volume (coefficient -3.35, 95% CI -27.8 to 21.1, p=0.79), pseudoaneurysm formation (aOR 0.75, 95% CI 0.44-1.29, p=0.30), or hospital length of stay (coefficient 3.11, 95% CI -0.12 to 6.33, p = 0.06). This nationwide study highlights current TXA practices in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma. No statistically significant associations between TXA administration and mortality or transfusion requirements were identified. Further adequately powered prospective studies are warranted to clarify the effectiveness of TXA in pediatric trauma.

articles.title: SEPSIS-INDUCED COAGULOPATHY ATTENUATES THE PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF THE HEMOGLOBIN-ALBUMIN-LYMPHOCYTE-PLATELET (HALP) SCORE IN SEPSIS.
articles.abstract: The hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score predicts outcomes in sepsis, but its platelet denominator is also a core component of sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC), and may distort its prognostic meaning. We examined whether SIC modifies HALP's association with 28-day mortality. We analyzed 6,218 adults meeting Sepsis-3 criteria in MIMIC-IV. HALP was calculated from first ICU measurements; SIC was defined by the 2017 ISTH criteria (score ≥4). Analyses included multivariable regression, interaction testing, propensity-score methods, and platelet-independent coagulopathy definitions, and evaluation of modified HALP (m-HALP; platelets in the numerator). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 25.6%; SIC incidence was 26.1%. HALP showed a J-shaped association with mortality (P for nonlinearity <0.001). The lowest quartile independently predicted death (adjusted OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.20-1.70; HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.10-1.39). This association persisted in non-SIC patients (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.28-1.79) but was attenuated and non-significant in SIC patients (OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.82-1.60; interaction P=0.006). Albumin carried HALP's discrimination in non-SIC patients, whereas platelets dominated in SIC (OR 0.51 per SD, P=0.001). When coagulopathy was redefined without platelets, the modification was no longer significant (P=0.295), indicating it partly reflects the shared platelet component. m-HALP was inversely associated with mortality in both strata (interaction P=0.691). Results were robust to weighting, 90-day mortality, and alternative Cox models. HALP is an independent prognostic marker mainly in septic patients without coagulopathy; once SIC develops, thrombocytopenia both raises mortality risk and arithmetically inflates HALP. Coagulation status should be assessed before HALP-based risk stratification; m-HALP may offer a platelet-consistent alternative.

articles.title: Consensus-derived clinical sepsis profiles and mortality across six international cohorts.
articles.abstract: Clinical phenotyping may help characterize sepsis heterogeneity, but the applicability of derived profiles across healthcare settings remains uncertain. We evaluated consensus-derived clinical profiles and their associations with mortality across six international cohorts. We analyzed 62,458 adults from six critical care databases in four countries. In the MIMIC-IV discovery cohort (n = 28,733), six clustering algorithms were applied to 24 routinely available clinical variables to derive consensus profiles. The profiles were assigned in five external cohorts using fixed discovery-cohort templates. We examined clinical characteristics, mortality associations, and exploratory treatment-outcome associations. Three profiles were selected based on the Calinski-Harabasz peak and clinical interpretability. Profiles 1, 2, and 3 comprised 32.6%, 20.0%, and 47.4% of the discovery cohort, with in-hospital mortality of 30.3%, 13.8%, and 9.3%, respectively. Profile 1 showed greater multiorgan dysfunction, Profile 2 relatively preserved hemodynamics, and Profile 3 greater ventilatory support with less extrapulmonary dysfunction. Profile 1 had the highest mortality in all five external cohorts, with a decreasing mortality gradient across profiles in most cohorts. After adjustment for age and SOFA score, Profile 3 was associated with lower 1-year mortality than Profile 1 (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.57-0.67). Treatment-outcome associations were exploratory. Consensus-derived profiles characterized clinically interpretable patterns of sepsis heterogeneity with mortality differences across the evaluated cohorts. These findings support further evaluation of clinical profiling for risk stratification and phenotype-informed research.

articles.title: Beyond 28-Day Mortality: The Unfinished Story of Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Survivorship.

Variation in Pediatric Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Survival After In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Development and Validation of a Survival Model for Risk-Standardized Survival Rates: An Analysis of the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization Registry.
articles.abstract: To develop and internally validate a multivariable prediction model for survival to hospital discharge after pediatric extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and to use this model to derive risk-standardized survival rates (RSSRs) and quantify between-hospital variation in outcomes. Retrospective multicenter cohort study. Hospitals contributing to the Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) registry between 2020 and 2023. Children (< 18 yr) treated with ECPR for IHCA. None. Eligible patients were identified from the ELSO Registry and split into derivation (N = 1060) and validation (N = 317) cohorts using a hospital-stratified split to preserve within-hospital clustering. Survival prediction models were derived using penalized logistic regression with the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. A full-event model incorporating 14 routinely available clinical variables demonstrated fair discrimination (area under the curve, 0.728 in the derivation cohort and 0.678 in the validation cohort) and good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio, 0.995; Brier score, 0.222 in the validation cohort). This model was embedded in a multilevel logistic regression model to generate hospital-level RSSRs for centers reporting five or more ECPR cases. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio, which was 1.30 (95% CI, 1.11-1.93), indicating significant differences in survival likelihood between centers after adjusting for patient-level risk. In a large, international cohort of pediatric ECPR patients, we developed and internally validated a clinically interpretable model for survival to hospital discharge. The model performance as a discriminator likely limits its use as a standalone tool for clinical decision-making. However, strong internal calibration allowed for determination of hospital-level RSSRs, which revealed significant inter-hospital variability. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of developing a risk-adjustment model capable of estimating hospital-level RSSRs. Additional external validation and evaluation of residual case-mix differences are needed before such models can be used for benchmarking across pediatric ECPR centers.

Fatal Opioid-Like Toxidrome Associated With a 7-Hydroxymitragynine Kratom Product.
articles.abstract: Kratom (Mitragyna speciosa) use has increased in the United States, with the market shifting from traditional leaf preparations to concentrated products containing concentrated or chemically processed alkaloids such as 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-HMG) and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl. These formulations may deliver supraphysiologic opioid-receptor agonist doses with poorly characterized toxicity. A 42-year-old man was found dead at home after reportedly ingesting 3 tablets of a commercial "7-HMG" product and several beers. Postmortem examination revealed purge fluid at the mouth and nose, severe bilateral pulmonary edema, distended bladder, and no evidence of trauma or injection drug use. Quantitative analysis of the remaining tablet showed 29 mg 7-HMG and 0.58 mg mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, with minimal mitragynine. Postmortem blood contained 37.3 ng/mL 7-HMG and 76 ng/mL mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, whereas gabapentin and other medications were present at subtherapeutic concentrations. Compared with an estimated 1 to 4.5 mg 7-HMG in a typical high dose of dried kratom leaf powder, this ingestion delivered approximately 87 mg 7-HMG (19-fold to 87-fold greater 7-HMG exposure than a high-dose botanical leaf preparation). Given the high μ-opioid receptor activity of 7-HMG and its in vivo conversion to the even more potent opioid agonist mitragynine pseudoindoxyl, the postmortem findings are most consistent with a fatal opioid-like toxidrome associated with exposure to concentrated kratom alkaloids. This case illustrates the emerging risk posed by new kratom-branded products containing purified or chemically enriched alkaloids at doses far exceeding traditional preparations.

Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes. Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings? We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes. Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p < 0.001). In the peri-diagnostic period, ILD clinic care was associated with higher adjusted odds of chest CT imaging (OR 2.51, 2.07-3.05) and antifibrotic therapy (OR 1.54, 1.32-1.80), and lower odds of lung biopsy (OR 0.47, 0.32-0.68). ILD clinic care was associated with a lower adjusted hazards of all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.46, 0.42-0.51), emergency department visit (HR 0.68, 0.59-0.78), and death (HR 0.57, 0.45-0.72). P-value <0.001 for all. Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved. Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD? Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency. The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]). Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.

articles.title: Traumatic Emergency Thoracotomy for Resuscitation in Shock (TETRiS): a national service evaluation of resuscitative thoracotomy practice outside the operating theatre.
articles.abstract: Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) is performed in patients with traumatic cardiac arrest or peri-arrest to treat potentially reversible causes of circulatory collapse. Optimal patient selection and timing remain uncertain, and existing evidence is largely retrospective, often excluding prehospital deaths. This prospective service evaluation examined contemporary RT practice and outcomes across a national major trauma system, including prehospital and emergency department settings. Prospective 12-month observational study across 20 UK Helicopter Emergency Medical Services and 26 Major Trauma Centre Emergency Departments, using the PHOTON, TERN, and NaTRIC research networks. A total of 116 patients underwent RT, of which 82 (70.7%) were performed prehospital. Median age was 30 years, 97 patients (83.6%) were male, and 81 (69.8%) sustained penetrating injury. Suspected cardiac tamponade was the most common indication for RT (72/116 [62.1%]), although operative findings demonstrated exsanguinating haemorrhage in 82 patients (70.7%). Overall, 50 patients (43.1%) achieved return of spontaneous circulation and eight (6.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Survival was strongly associated with pathophysiological cause, duration of arrest, and physiological state at the time of intervention, with substantially better outcomes observed in patients with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination. Patients undergoing emergency department RT demonstrated shorter arrest durations, more favourable physiology, and higher survival than those undergoing prehospital RT. There were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest. In this prospective national evaluation of RT practice, outcomes were strongly associated with the pathophysiological cause and duration of arrest, and the residual physiology present at the time of intervention. The most favourable outcomes were observed in patients with cardiac tamponade and those undergoing RT before irreversible physiological deterioration.

Associations Between Diagnostic Blood-Based Biomarkers and Neuroimaging Findings in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) is a prevalent and resource-intensive injury in the emergency department (ED). The blood-based biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin c-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) have demonstrated diagnostic potential for acute structural brain injury. Our objective was to clinically validate a US Food and Drug Administration-approved plasma test to aid in the identification of intracranial injury in patients with mTBI presenting to the ED and assess its integration with existing protocols. This single-center validation study enrolled 104 adult patients with suspected mTBI undergoing head computed tomography (CT) for evaluation between October 2023 and June 2024 at a Level I trauma center. Peripheral blood draw was completed within 12 hours postinjury and processed at the hospital clinical laboratory. Sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values for the test were calculated and compared with a standard clinical decision rule (Canadian Head CT Rule). ED length of stay and diagnostic turnaround times were examined. Within the cohort (n=104), 83 patients had elevated biomarker levels (GFAP >30 pg/mL or UCH-L1 >360 pg/mL), and 11 patients had intracranial injury identified on CT. The combination plasma test demonstrated high sensitivity (0.91 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.59 to 1.00]) but low specificity (0.22 [95% CI 0.14 to 0.31]) for predicting intracranial injury on CT with low positive predictive value (0.12 [95% CI 0.06 to 0.21]) and high negative predictive value (0.95 [95% CI 0.76 to 1.00]). These findings are consistent with prior studies (pooled sensitivity 0.97 [95% CI 0.95 to 0.98]; specificity 0.28 [95% CI 0.23 to 0.34]). False-positive cases (78%) were older than true-negative cases (median 72 years [interquartile range (IQR) 54 to 83] versus 58.5 years [IQR 38.25 to 66]). Median turnaround time for the GFAP/UCH-L1 test was 2 hours faster than head CT (1.09 hours [IQR 0.87 to 1.65] versus 3.28 hours [IQR 2.37 to 4.70]). Blood biomarkers for mTBI have potential as an initial rule-out tool for intracranial injury prior to obtaining CT imaging; however, large multicenter studies are needed to clarify its impact on ED resource utilization, length of stay, and acute and long-term costs and benefits to patients and health care systems.

articles.title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Use and Objective Documentation Effort Among Emergency Physicians.
articles.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes ("AI scribes") are purported to reduce emergency department (ED) documentation burden, but ED evidence is largely single-site, uncontrolled, or self-reported, with exposure inferred rather than measured. We evaluated AI scribe use among attending emergency physicians across a multisite network, with exposure and outcomes read directly from the electronic health record. Across 20 EDs (3 academic and 17 community), AI scribe use was flagged per note from the patient consent statement within the ED note. Analyses were restricted to attending physicians and, to isolate the physician's own documentation, excluded teaching encounters and attestation notes identified from standardized attestation text. Endpoints, computed over the mature-adoption window (December 2025 onward, when Epic audit-log data are retained), were active time in the note (primary), note length, note-start time, completion lag, and 72-hour ED return. Within-physician models (physician and calendar-month fixed effects, clustered by physician) compared each adopter's AI-scribed notes with their own unassisted notes, adjusting only for pre-exposure case mix. Among 275 attending physicians, 31% of encounters were AI-scribed. Physicians spent less active time in AI-scribed notes (median 10.0 versus 12.5 min-2.4 minutes after adjustment), started them about 15 minutes later (median 31 versus 17 minutes after first seeing the patient, and produced notes about 14% longer [median 5,220 versus 4,468 characters; within-physician +629 characters]). Note completion was not delayed (-6 minutes), and 72-hour ED return was not increased (-0.8 percentage point; 95% confidence interval -1.5 to -0.1). Among emergency physicians, AI scribe use was associated with less active time in the note, deferred note-start, and longer notes, without delaying completion or increasing short-term returns, with effect sizes consistent with ambulatory randomized data.

articles.title: Who's on Airway? Trainee Tracheal Intubation Frequency and Outcomes Within the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine (NEAR4PEM).
articles.abstract: We aimed to describe trainee performance and tracheal intubation outcomes in academic pediatric emergency departments. We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study of intubations performed between January 2021 and December 2023, using data from the National Emergency Airway Registry for Pediatric Emergency Medicine. Eligible encounters included children who underwent intubation with the first-attempt proceduralist identified as an emergency medicine resident, a pediatric resident, or a pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellow. The primary outcome was first-attempt success. The secondary outcome was adverse airway outcomes, defined as desaturation or tracheal intubation-associated adverse events. We compared intubation outcomes across trainee groups. Over the 1,404 encounters during the study period, 642 (48%) were primary intubations performed on pediatric patients by an emergency medicine, pediatric or PEM trainee. A total of 343 (53%) first attempts were by emergency medicine residents, 254 (40%) by PEM fellows, and 45 (7%) by pediatric residents. The overall trainee first-attempt success rate was 471/642 (73%). First-attempt success by emergency medicine residents (75%) and PEM fellows (74%) were similar, and higher than first-attempt success by pediatric residents (58%). After accounting for potential confounders, there was no difference between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows in first-attempt success (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56 to 1.28) or adverse airway outcome (aOR 1.4, 95% CI 0.96 to 2.18). In adjusted analysis, pediatric residents had a lower first-attempt success (aOR 0.41, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.82) and a higher adverse airway outcome (aOR 2.14, 95% CI 1.08 to 4.27) than emergency medicine residents. There was no difference in first-attempt success and adverse airway outcomes between emergency medicine residents and PEM fellows. Pediatric residents have lower first-attempt success and higher adverse airway outcomes than emergency medicine residents.

An anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide augments whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock in a rodent polytrauma model.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Severe trauma induces a cytokine storm that is associated with impaired resuscitation and recovery. We investigated the impact of AQB-565, an anti-inflammatory melanocortin fusion polypeptide, as a novel treatment adjunct for whole blood resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock using a rat polytrauma shock model. Hemorrhagic shock with polytrauma was induced in 64 Sprague-Dawley rats. The rats were randomized to receive one of four intravenous treatments at 15 minutes posthemorrhage (T15): saline control, AQB-565, tranexamic acid (TXA), or combined AQB-565+ TXA. The rats were given autologous transfusion of shed whole blood at 60 minutes and as needed thereafter to achieve mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 60 mm Hg for up to 3 hours. Survival, hemodynamics, cytokine profiles, and hemorrhage volumes were compared between groups. There was a significant overall effect of treatment group on MAP (two-way rmANOVA p=0.02) that coincided with blood transfusion. MAP was significantly increased at T105 with AQB-565+TXA versus saline control (p=0.046). Inflammatory plasma cytokines, including interleukin-6, were significantly decreased with AQB-565 versus control groups (ANOVA p values ≤0.01). Seventeen (26.6%) rats died before 3 hours. There was a trend towards increased survival for treatments containing AQB-565 versus controls that was not statistically significant (Kaplan-Meier log rank p=0.06). A melanocortin pathway-activating polypeptide suppressed inflammation and improved hemodynamic response to whole blood transfusion in this hemorrhagic shock model.

Pediatric Musculoskeletal Infections: Who Needs a Tap or MRI? From Kocher to PEMCRC.
articles.abstract: Bacterial musculoskeletal infections (MSKIs), including septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, and pyomyositis, are challenging diagnoses to make in pediatric emergency medicine because their presentation frequently overlaps with more common conditions, including transient synovitis, Lyme arthritis, reactive arthritis, and other inflammatory arthritides. While delayed diagnosis may result in significant morbidity, over-testing may expose children to invasive procedures, advanced imaging, sedation, hospitalization, and unnecessary antimicrobial therapy. Pediatric emergency clinicians must therefore balance the competing risks of missed infection and excessive diagnostic evaluation and treatment. Numerous tools exist to aid clinicians, including blood biomarkers-white blood cell (WBC) count, absolute neutrophil count (ANC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and procalcitonin (PCT). However, blood biomarkers have limited diagnostic accuracy when used in isolation. To address this limitation, clinical prediction tools that combine laboratory values with clinical features to stratify risk have been developed. In this review, we summarize the data for clinically available biomarkers and clinical prediction tools for the evaluation of pediatric bacterial MSKIs and discuss their practical application, limitations, and integration into clinical decision-making in the emergency department (ED). Ultimately, we provide a framework to help pediatric emergency clinicians identify children who require advanced testing and interventions while avoiding unnecessary evaluation and treatment in low-risk patients.

Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated. Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses? We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up. Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline. Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.

articles.title: European Society of Intensive Care Medicine consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract: A human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit (ICU) aims to integrate person-centred care, communication, emotional support, equity, and collaboration into ICU environments. The European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) developed a consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU following a systematic, multi-phase, evidence-informed methodology incorporating the views of ICU professionals, academics, and patient and family representatives. This international multidisciplinary panel of 46 members conducted rapid reviews addressing 20 Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes (PICO) questions across six domains: person-centred care; communication and transparency; emotional well-being; equity, diversity, and inclusion; ICU environment; technology and innovation. Based on the evidence synthesis, 53 draft statements were developed and evaluated through a two-round eDelphi study. The final set of statements was discussed and ratified at an expert consensus meeting with the initial panel of experts and with patients and family representatives. A total of 201 international stakeholders participated in round 1 and 149 in round 2. Members of the expert consensus meeting ultimately endorsed 43 consensus statements. Key recommendations supported flexible family visitation, structured interdisciplinary communication, empathy-based staff training, psychological support for patients and ICU professionals, culturally responsive care, environmental interventions to improve sleep and reduce delirium, and the integration of digital supported technologies. The consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians with evidence-informed directions to deliver high-quality practice across diverse ICU settings. By prioritising person-centred care, communication, inclusivity, and well-being alongside responsible technological innovation, the experiences and outcomes of patients, families, and ICU professionals may improve.

Preliminary Exploration of the Hepatoprotective Effect of Nanocrystalline Curcumin Against Traumatic Hemorrhagic Shock-Induced Liver Injury in a Desert Dry-Heat Environment: A Network Pharmacology-Based Study.
articles.abstract: Traumatic hemorrhagic shock (THS) under desert dry-heat conditions can exacerbate secondary liver injury, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic interventions. This study investigated the protective effects of nanocrystalline curcumin (NC-Cur) against THS-induced liver injury in a desert dry-heat environment and explored its potential molecular mechanisms. Network pharmacology, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses, and protein-protein interaction network analysis were used to identify candidate targets. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations examined curcumin-protein interactions. Forty male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control, model, solvent, or NC-Cur treatment groups (n = 10 each). The model, solvent, and treatment groups underwent traumatic hemorrhagic shock under desert dry-heat conditions. Hepatic injury was assessed by histopathology, serum aminotransferases, inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and Western blotting. Network analysis identified 116 overlapping targets, with heat shock protein 90 alpha A1 (HSP90AA1), AKT serine/threonine kinase 1 (AKT1), and B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) prioritized as the core targets. Docking predicted favorable interactions with all three proteins, while molecular dynamics simulations supported stable binding between curcumin and HSP90AA1. Compared with untreated model rats, NC-Cur-treated rats showed attenuated hepatic histopathological injury, reduced alanine and aspartate aminotransferases, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-1β, and malondialdehyde, and increased superoxide dismutase. Western blotting indicated reduced HSP90AA1 and increased phosphorylated AKT1 expression after NC-Cur treatment, with changes also observed in BCL-2 expression. These findings suggest that NC-Cur may alleviate liver injury associated with THS under desert dry-heat conditions in male rats, potentially involving HSP90AA1-AKT1-BCL-2-related signaling.

articles.title: Tongue capillary refill time and imaging parameters for acute coronary syndrome identification: A prospective ED study.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Rapid identification of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain remains challenging. Tongue capillary refill time (CRT) and tongue imaging may reflect systemic perfusion, but their value in ACS is unknown. To evaluate the diagnostic performance of standardized tongue-derived perfusion, macroscopic, and imaging parameters for identifying ACS. This prospective observational study enrolled 208 consecutive adult ED patients presenting with chest pain. Standardized tongue imaging and tongue CRT were assessed. A separate 20-patient pilot assessed interobserver reliability using ICC and kappa coefficients. Blinded ACS adjudication used clinical findings, serial high-sensitivity troponin measurements, electrocardiography, imaging studies, specialist consultations, and follow-up data. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Among 208 patients, 61 (29.3%) had ACS: 16 STEMI, 41 NSTEMI, and four unstable angina cases. Tongue CRT was significantly prolonged in ACS patients (2.6 [2.2-2.9] vs. 1.3 [1.1-1.6] seconds; p<0.001). Tongue CRT demonstrated excellent discrimination for ACS (AUC 0.941, 95% CI 0.903-0.980), outperforming the HEART score (0.860), admission troponin (0.831), and TIMI score (0.788). A CRT threshold ≥2s yielded 86.9% sensitivity and 93.2% specificity. Tongue CRT and macroscopically dry tongue remained associated with ACS after adjustment (both p<0.001). Quantitative RGB and HSV parameters showed no significant between-group differences. Standardized tongue CRT showed excellent discrimination for ACS in this cohort, in which most ACS cases were myocardial infarction. Its diagnostic value in unstable angina and incremental clinical utility remain unestablished. External validation is required before routine clinical use.

articles.title: An original closed reduction technique for acute shoulder dislocation: The FEAT method.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: The objective of this study was to introduce a novel closed reduction technique, termed the FEAT (Fixation, External rotation, Alignment, Traction) method, for anterior shoulder dislocations and to evaluate its effectiveness, speed, reliability, and safety. This prospective study enrolled 30 patients presenting with anterior glenohumeral dislocation at the Emergency or Orthopedics outpatient department of Hubei Provincial Hospital. Closed reduction was performed using the FEAT method without administering analgesics, muscle relaxants, or anesthetics. Only a single reduction attempt was permitted per patient. The time required for successful reduction was recorded, and patient-reported pain intensity during the procedure was assessed using a visual analog scale (VAS) ranging from 0 to 10. All 30 patients experienced successful reduction on the first attempt. The average time required for successful reduction was 54.3 s, with a mean VAS pain score of 3.67 during the procedure. The FEAT method is an effective, rapid, and minimally painful technique for anterior shoulder dislocation reduction. Its simplicity and ease of mastery support its widespread clinical adoption.

articles.title: [Nursing competencies in ECMO care: a scoping review].
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is used in cases of refractory cardiac or pulmonary failure and places high demands on the treatment team, particularly on nursing staff, whose required competencies have scarcely been described in German-speaking countries. The primary aim was to map the international evidence on nursing competencies in the care of adult ECMO patients. Secondary aims included identifying specialised nursing roles and drawing implications for the German-speaking countries. The scoping review was conducted in accordance with the guidelines of the Joanna Briggs Institute and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses- Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). The literature search was carried out in MEDLINE, CINAHL and Scopus, as well as in reference lists. German- and English-language primary studies published between 2009 and May 2026 were included. A total of n = 14 studies were included, comprising n = 7 qualitative (n = 6 [semi-structured] interview studies, n = 1 focus group interview) and n = 7 quantitative (n = 3 cross-sectional studies, n = 1 Delphi survey, n = 1 prospective cohort study, n = 1 prospective observational study, and n = 1 quasi-experimental study) studies. Based on the identified evidence, a multidimensional competency profile for ECMO nursing care can be described, including the necessary knowledge, practical skills, and professional attitudes. In addition, specialised nursing roles were identified. No studies meeting the inclusion criteria were identified for German-speaking countries. A multidimensional competency profile emerges that is internationally anchored in specialised nursing roles; however, empirical data, role profiles and structured qualification pathways are lacking in German-speaking countries.

articles.title: One-year mortality following emergency department visits for stimulant toxicity.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Rising stimulant-related overdose deaths and emergency department (ED) utilization highlight the need to better characterize outcomes following ED encounters for stimulant toxicity. We sought to determine one-year mortality after ED discharge for stimulant toxicity and to characterize the causes of death. This retrospective cohort study used a linked statewide database of ED and hospital discharge records and death records. Patients discharged from the ED with a primary diagnosis of stimulant toxicity, identified by International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes, were included. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within one year of ED discharge, estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. A secondary reference analysis was performed among patients with ED visits for acute opioid toxicity to contextualize mortality estimates against a population previously associated with elevated post-discharge mortality. A total of 2356 patients met inclusion criteria. One-year mortality was 2.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.6-2.8%). Among patients who died within one year, median age at the index visit was 35 years and median time to death was 118 days (interquartile range [IQR] 63-228 days). Overdose accounted for 67% of deaths, with opioids implicated in 54% and combined opioid-stimulant involvement in 37%. In the secondary reference cohort of 1665 opioid-related ED visits, one-year mortality was 6.9% (95% CI 5.8-8.3%). Patients with ED encounters for stimulant toxicity experienced substantial one-year mortality in a relatively young population. Subsequent deaths were predominantly overdose-related and frequently opioid-involved, supporting consideration of opioid-focused harm-reduction interventions in this population.

articles.title: Disparities in investigation of physical abuse among trauma patients.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Physical abuse is a significant public health issue in the United States, leading to poor health outcomes such as chronic illness, depression, and substance abuse. Research regarding how the medical system addresses physical abuse in the overall adult population is scarce. The objective of this study was to assess disparities in investigation of physical abuse among adult trauma patients. This is a retrospective analysis of the 2017-2019 American College of Surgeons-Trauma Quality Program database. This study included all adult patients (≥18 years) who had a report of physical abuse by the medical team to authorities. Chi square and multivariate analysis were applied where appropriate to assess which characteristics showed disparities in investigation rate. On univariate analysis, there were disparities with regard to age, mechanism, race, ethnicity, payment method, and mental health or substance use disorder. On multivariate analysis, male sex, non-penetrating trauma, age ≥70, American Indian race, and presence of a mental health disorder were associated with decreased odds of investigation. Non-elderly adult patients made up a disproportionate amount of abuse victims. This study shows significant disparities in the escalation of a physical abuse report to an official investigation in the trauma setting. The authors recommend increased advocacy and resource allocation for these vulnerable populations in the clinical setting as well as further research regarding to what extent patient choice versus discretion of authorities influences these disparities. The authors also recommend a larger research focus on non-elderly adult victims of abuse.

Association of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Radiographic Findings Identified by Machine Learning and Outcomes of Patients Receiving Invasive Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.abstract: To determine whether predictions from a deep learning model that identifies acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) findings on chest radiographs (CXRs) can also predict clinical outcomes beyond traditional indicators of hypoxemia and illness severity. Retrospective cohort study. Single academic medical center. None. Adult patients with CXRs performed at the time of invasive mechanical ventilation initiation. We applied a deep learning model that was previously trained to identify bilateral airspace opacities consistent with ARDS to CXRs of 6591 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. The resulting ARDS-CXR scores were evaluated for their ability to discriminate risk of 28-day mortality and their association with 28-day mortality and time to extubation after adjusting for a patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV. The median ARDS-CXR score was -2.09, corresponding to an ARDS probability of 15%, and 1089 (17%) patients had a positive score, corresponding to an ARDS probability above 50%. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 35.1% among patients with a positive score and 13.5% among patients with a negative score. ARDS-CXR scores below the ARDS threshold also stratified risk, with mortality increasing from 12.8% at a score of -2 to 19.9% at -1 and 27.5% at 0. The ARDS-CXR score area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve was 0.68 (95% CI, 0.66-0.70) for predicting 28-day mortality, whereas the Pao2/Fio2 AUROC was 0.64 (95% CI, 0.62-0.66). After adjusting for either the patient's Pao2/Fio2 or Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation-IV, a 1-point increase in the ARDS-CXR score was significantly associated with higher 28-day mortality or prolonged time to extubation. A deep learning-derived ARDS-CXR score quantifying radiographic findings of ARDS independently predicted mortality and ventilator outcomes beyond hypoxemia and illness severity. Algorithmically derived markers of lung injury severity from chest imaging could be used to support clinical care decisions, predictive enrichment in research studies, or incorporated into a future ARDS definition.

articles.title: Brachial-to-Radial Pressure Gradient in Critically Ill Patients Treated With Vasoactive Agents: A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Polish Perioperative and Critical Care Research Group (PERI-CRIT)
articles.abstract: To determine the incidence of a significant noninvasive brachial-to-radial arterial pressure gradient (NIBR-APG) and its clinical associations in critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents. Prospective, multicenter, observational study. Thirteen ICUs in Poland. Adult ICU patients with radial arterial catheters receiving vasoactive agents hospitalized between April 2025 and July 2025. None. Invasive radial mean arterial pressure (MAP) and noninvasive brachial MAP were measured twice and averaged. A NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg was predefined as clinically significant. Baseline characteristics, hemodynamic variables, and outcomes were recorded. Among 303 patients, 49.5% were surgical admissions and 33.3% had septic shock. The median NIBR-APG was 4.5 mm Hg (interquartile range, 0.0-10.0 mm Hg). Fifty-six patients (18.4%) exhibited a NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg. Compared with patients without a significant gradient, these patients received higher norepinephrine-equivalent doses (0.23 vs. 0.10 µg/kg/min), had higher Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores (11 vs. 10), prolonged capillary refill time (3.0 vs. 2.5 s), and higher lactate concentrations (2.7 vs. 1.3 mmol/L). In multivariable analysis, only vasoactive drug dose was independently associated with NIBR-APG greater than 11 mm Hg (odds ratio, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.12-2.52). ICU mortality was higher in patients with significant gradients (48.0% vs. 30.1%). Nearly one in five critically ill patients receiving vasoactive agents demonstrated a clinically significant NIBR-APG. The presence of this gradient was independently associated with higher vasoactive drug requirements and was accompanied by greater illness severity and higher ICU mortality.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Tracheal Intubation-Associated Cardiac Arrest in 2015-2023: A Report From the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children Multicenter Registry.
authors: National Emergency Airway Registry for Children (NEAR4KIDS) investigators as a subgroup of Pediatric Acute Lung Injury and Sepsis Investigators (PALISI)
articles.abstract: To determine the contemporary incidence of tracheal intubation-associated cardiac arrest (TI-CA) in critically ill children and identify potentially modifiable factors to prevent TI-CA in PICUs and pediatric cardiac ICUs (PCICUs). Retrospective cohort study. Seventy international PICUs and PCICUs. Critically ill children requiring tracheal intubation in PICUs and PCICUs. Tracheal intubation data were prospectively collected for all initial intubations in 68 PICUs and PCICUs from January 2015 to December 2023 using the National Emergency Airway Registry for Children registry. TI-CA was defined as CA occurrence or receipt of chest compressions for at least 1 minute within 20 minutes of endotracheal tube placement. TI during ongoing cardiopulmonary resuscitation was not considered TI-CA. A total of 27,773 TIs were evaluated, with TI-CA reported in 1.2% (n = 331). Pre-TI oxygenation failure and shock were associated with higher odds of TI-CA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.29; 95% CI, 1.81-2.89 and aOR, 4.67; 95% CI, 3.68-5.92, respectively). Each additional TI attempt required was associated with increased odds of TI-CA (aOR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.56-1.85, for each attempt). Use of ketamine (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.49-0.82), propofol (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.27-0.72), neuromuscular blockade (aOR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.49-0.91), and video laryngoscopy (aOR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.6-0.97) were associated with lower odds of TI-CA. Mediation analysis indicated that 13% of video laryngoscopy's protective effect was due to a reduction in TI attempt counts. The protective effects of ketamine, propofol, and neuromuscular blockade were minimally mediated by reduced TI attempt counts (5%, 4%, and 7%). TI-CA occurred in 1.2% of TIs performed in the PICUs. Odds of TI-CA increased incrementally with successive TI attempts. Video laryngoscopy was protective against TI-CA. Mediation analysis revealed that reduced TI attempts accounted for 13% of the protective benefit associated with video laryngoscopy.

articles.title: Non-Diagnostic Does Not Mean Non-Malignant: Outcomes and Predictors of Malignancy Following Nondiagnostic Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy.
Adherence to Non-Invasive Ventilation in a Provincial Cohort of Children.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) adherence is critical to its effectiveness, yet no standardized pediatric definition of "optimal" adherence exists, and population-level data are scarce. What are adherence patterns to NIV in children, and which factors are associated with adherence in a provincial longitudinal cohort? Canadian retrospective longitudinal cohort study linking records from the Ontario Ventilator Equipment Pool to health administrative databases. We identified children <18 years prescribed NIV with telemonitoring (2020 to 2022) and ≥1 month of data. The adherence definitions explored were the adult definition of ≥4 hours/day (primary) and measures of any daily use, daily NIV hours, and data missingness ("days not used" = 0 hours recorded; "days no data" = no signal). Mixed-effects regression models were used to explore adherence factors. We included 237 children (mean age 12.9 years; 61% male) with 3,685 person-months of NIV data (median 13 [IQR 8-24]). Across person-months, mean adherence by the ≥4-hours/day definition was 69.6%. Child-level monthly mean (SD) adherence was 59% (32%) by this definition, and 68% (26%) for any use. Mean (SD) daily use when used was 7.5 (3.2) hours. Monthly "days not used" and "no data" averaged 5.1 (6.4) and 4.4 (5.0) days, respectively. Greater adherence was associated with younger age (2-percentage-point decrease per year increase; 95% CI, 1-3), having ≥3 complex chronic conditions vs none (14 percentage-points higher; 95% CI, 3-26), and longer time prescribed NIV (2-percentage-point increase per year; 95% CI, 1-3). NIV adherence was moderate across definitions, with higher adherence among younger children, greater medical complexity, and those using therapy longer, highlighting the need for pediatric-specific adherence targets and home NIV support strategies.

articles.title: Comparison of delivery room wrist versus earlobe pulse oximetry in newborns: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition. Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications. Ninety-six neonates were randomized, with 48 in each group. Time from completion of sensor application to reliable signal was similar between ear and wrist groups (67.1±41.4 vs 74.5±48.2 seconds; mean difference -7.4 seconds; 95% CI -25.6 to 10.8; P=0.42). Sensor application time was shorter in ear group (mean difference -16.3 seconds; 95% CI -17.7 to -14.9; P<0.001), resulting in shorter time from birth to reliable signal (mean difference -28.8 seconds; 95% CI -53.9 to -3.7; P=0.02). Perfusion index was lower, and reapplication rates were higher in ear group. Time to reliable signal acquisition after probe placement did not differ between the earlobe and wrist. Further studies using neonatal-specific ear probes are warranted.

articles.title: β-Blockade reprograms trauma-induced changes in bone marrow exosomal microRNAs.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Severe trauma produces sustained sympathetic activation that contributes to bone marrow dysfunction, impaired hematopoiesis, and persistent injury-associated anemia. Although β-adrenergic blockade improves bone marrow recovery after injury, the downstream mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol reprograms trauma-induced bone marrow extracellular vesicle (EV) microRNA (miRNA) expression toward restoration of hematopoietic homeostasis. Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized to naïve, polytrauma (PT), PT plus propranolol (PT+BB), PT with chronic restraint stress (PTRS), or PTRS plus propranolol (PTRS+BB) groups (n=6-8 per group). Propranolol (10 mg/kg intraperitoneally) was administered daily. On day 7, complete blood counts were obtained, and bone marrow-derived EV miRNAs were profiled using the NanoString nCounter platform. Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using an absolute log2 fold change ≥1.5 and p<0.05. Predicted pathways were assessed using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, and miR-125b-5p was validated by quantitative PCR. PT altered 45 EV miRNAs compared with naïve animals, including suppression of miRNAs involved in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and erythropoiesis. Chronic restraint stress amplified this response, with 93 differentially expressed miRNAs following PTRS. Propranolol altered 12 miRNAs after PT and 43 after PTRS, increasing hematopoietic regulatory miRNAs, including miR-125b-5p, while suppressing several stress- and inflammation-associated miRNAs. Pathway analysis identified alterations in NOTCH, RUNX1, PTEN, thyroid receptor/retinoid X receptor, and histone modification signaling. Quantitative PCR confirmed a 2.4-fold increase in EV miR-125b-5p following propranolol in PTRS animals (p=0.018). Trauma and persistent adrenergic stress broadly remodel bone marrow EV miRNA signaling. β-Adrenergic blockade selectively reprograms these networks toward pathways associated with hematopoietic recovery, identifying EV miRNAs as potential mediators of posttraumatic bone marrow dysfunction. Not applicable-Animal research.
